version.changelog:
make-to-markdown v1.0.0

- Initial release of the make-to-markdown skill for industrial-grade RAG Markdown conversion.
- Supports converting PDF, Word (.docx/.doc), PowerPoint (.pptx/.ppt), Excel (.xlsx, .xls), HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, images (with EXIF/OCR), audio (with transcription), ZIP, YouTube links, and EPub to Markdown.
- Old Office formats (.doc/.ppt) are automatically preprocessed with Word/PowerPoint COM or LibreOffice.
- Automatic OS, version, and capability detection ensures best execution path per platform.
- Strict constraints for security: read-only source files, no cloud APIs, user confirmation on overwrites, robust batch operation confirmation, UTF-8 output, and local execution only.
- Unified conversion and post-processing pipeline managed through scripts/convert.py, handling dependencies, error fallback, and content cleaning.

llm.summary: This appears to be a genuine document-to-Markdown converter, but it automatically installs persistent dependencies and its scripts do not enforce some documented confirmation safeguards for overwrites and batch work.

dimensions.detail: The core behavior is coherent with the stated purpose: converting PDFs, Office files, spreadsheets, media, archives, and other inputs into Markdown using markitdown plus fallback converters.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill text requires confirmation before overwriting outputs and before recursive batch conversion, but convert.py overwrites the output path directly and batch_convert.py recursively processes matching files once invoked.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Normal conversion can run pip install and uv tool install --force for markitdown and many extras from public registries, without version pinning, hashes, or a separate explicit install step.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill is local-first and says not to upload document content, but it expands the local environment by installing broad optional packages, including network-capable YouTube transcript support, and invokes large external parsers such as Office COM or LibreOffice for legacy documents.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: There is no evidence of credential access, background workers, or hidden persistence, but dependency installation persists in the user's Python or uv tool environment beyond a single conversion.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with first-run network access and persistent package/tool installation. Prefer using it in a virtual environment or container, review output paths before running, avoid untrusted Office documents unless LibreOffice/Office is patched and sandboxed, and use a dedicated output directory for batch conversion.
llm.findings:
[AST4] expected: Subprocess use is expected for invoking pip, uv, markitdown, and LibreOffice in this conversion workflow, but the automatic package installation and external parser invocation create real host-side risk.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Automatic installation is disclosed, but it is broader than necessary for many single-file conversions and lacks user opt-in, pinning, or integrity controls.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The documentation mentions automatic dependency installation and batch conversion, but the strongest safety checkpoints are written as agent instructions rather than enforced by the scripts themselves.
